input.request: Audit the upload acceptance/continuation path before raising replicas from one to three. Inspect the producer, publisher, reader, storage contract and mount. Update docs/state-audit.md with the correct state classification, any necessary focused correction and targeted verification. Preserve an adequate placement; do not expand this into a full service redesign or upgrade Java.
input.prerequisites: Create an isolated fixture workspace from these exact files and provide the stateless-service-design skill plus file read/write tools. These are review excerpts and explicit adapter contracts, not a complete runnable application. Do not expose evaluator criteria.

fixtures.docs/upload-contract.md: POST /uploads returns 202 and an upload ID. After that response, the bytes must remain available for seven days and GET /uploads/{id} on any eligible replica must work despite loss of the accepting Pod. A fresh POST creates a new upload; request deduplication is outside this scoped review. Partial attempts that return no 202 may leave an orphan for the existing cleanup job. Staging has bounded cardinality/bytes and cleanup already; all replicas share the same durable catalog and blob namespace. The supplied storage adapter contract guarantees putAndAwaitDurability returns only after accepted blob durability/readability, and markAvailableCommitted returns only after the catalog entry is committed and visible to the readers. GET first reads this catalog and then the immutable blob. Java 17, no preview features; Kubernetes 1.34.
fixtures.deploy/pod-template.yaml:
spec:
  containers:
    - name: uploads
      image: example/uploads:review
      volumeMounts:
        - name: stage
          mountPath: /stage
  volumes:
    - name: stage
      emptyDir: {}
fixtures.docs/state-audit.md:
# Upload state audit

Proposal: increase replicas from one to three.
Current conclusion: /stage contains only temporary request data, so it creates no accepted-work dependency on one instance. The service can satisfy the upload contract after the accepting Pod is removed. No change to publication ordering is required.
Scope: the upload acceptance and continuation path only; no claim of completed capacity validation.

expected: Follow POST -> publishAsync -> in-memory executor -> publishCommitted, not only the Files/staging declaration.
Identify a window after 202 where /stage holds the only bytes and the only publication task is volatile. The local file/queue is authoritative for the promised accepted work during that phase.
Read the emptyDir mount: a container restart is not the same loss event as removing the Pod.
Correct the existing approval. GET on B or replacement of A before publication can violate the stated promise; one-replica success is insufficient.

Propose a sufficient focused ordering/recovery change: complete durable publication before 202, or establish a durable acceptance/replay handoff containing accessible bytes and metadata. Sticky routing or a longer graceful drain alone does not satisfy abrupt Pod-loss durability.
Name a discriminating check that blocks publication, observes 202 from A, removes A, then continues via B and checks the promised bytes/catalog outcome; use only an isolated authorized environment.
failures: Calls the bytes harmless merely because their filename or directory is temporary.
Treats background.submit success as durable acceptance.
Claims emptyDir loss on every container restart or assumes it survives Pod removal.
Adds affinity or Redis metadata while leaving acknowledged bytes solely on the lost Pod.
Only appends a caution and leaves the original approval unchanged.
Claims a real failure test or durability guarantee was executed from these review excerpts.
evaluator.walkthrough: Existing workflow steps 1/2/4/6, local-path rule and accepted-work shutdown rule identify the vulnerable acknowledgement phase and require a durable publication/handoff contract. Structured walkthrough only.
